dropped.checklist_item: - [ ] Make reconcile.py, apply_phase.py, and persist_phase.py load reconcile_helpers/pass_support under the SAME sys.modules key so they share one module instance.
evidence: reconcile.py:64 `_helpers = _load("rebar_reconciler.reconcile_helpers", "reconcile_helpers.py")`
reconcile.py:65 `_pass_support = _load("rebar_reconciler.pass_support", "pass_support.py")`
apply_phase.py:44 `_pass_support = lazy_load("pass_support", "pass_support.py")`
apply_phase.py:45 / persist_phase.py:50 `_helpers = lazy_load("reconcile_helpers", "reconcile_helpers.py")`
_loader.py:54 `if key in sys.modules: return sys.modules[key]` — cache is keyed on the exact string, so a fq key and a short key never collapse to one instance

Consequence: pass_support.SelectionStaleError / StatusMappingError have two distinct class objects; the code happens to survive only because __main__.py:240 catches via `type(exc).__name__ == "SelectionStaleError"` (name-based) and StatusMappingError is no longer caught anywhere
dropped.finding: reconcile.py now loads reconcile_helpers and pass_support under fully-qualified sys.modules keys (`rebar_reconciler.reconcile_helpers`, `rebar_reconciler.pass_support`), but apply_phase.py and persist_phase.py still load the same siblings under the short keys (`reconcile_helpers`, `pass_support`). Because lazy_load caches strictly by the exact key string, these modules are now executed and held as TWO distinct instances at runtime, where before this change reconcile.py used the short keys and shared one instance with the phase modules.
scenarios: Any future `except pass_support.SelectionStaleError`/`isinstance` check added across the reconcile↔apply_phase boundary would silently miss because the two instances have distinct classes
Double execution of pass_support.py / reconcile_helpers.py per process
dropped.suggested_fix: Pick one canonical key convention (the fully-qualified `rebar_reconciler.<name>`) and update apply_phase.py:44-45 and persist_phase.py:50 to use it too, so all three loads resolve to a single cached instance.
